title: destroy has no preview: nothing says what it will remove before it removes it
foundBy: session agent about to destroy one of two eight-member campaigns on a host where a third campaign belonged to someone else
details:
**The gap.** `cs-campaign create` takes `--dry-run` (*"resolve only; create nothing"*), and an operator can read back exactly what will be provisioned before spending anything. `destroy`, the one command in the surface that cannot be undone, has no equivalent. Its flags are `--force`, `--archive` and `--archive-output`. It loads the campaign's record, lists the live sandboxes, and destroys every member whose ref is present, last member first; with `--force` it asks nothing.

**Why it matters.** Destroying a campaign takes each member's machine with it, and with the machine everything that was never fetched or archived: uncommitted work, the member's out-of-tree output, its CLI session store. The playbook tells an operator to harvest first and to check rather than assume. The check an operator wants at that moment is the tool's own answer to *"which machines, exactly?"*. On a host that is running more than one campaign, possibly someone else's, they also want to ask *"and nothing else?"*. Today the only way to get it is to go around the tool, by listing the sandboxes and filtering by the campaign's group by hand. That is the operator re-deriving the member set the command already holds.

**What is asked for.** `destroy <campaign> --dry-run`: resolve and print, and remove nothing. It should name the group, and every member it would destroy, with its sandbox ref and whether that machine is present. It should name any member in the record that has no live machine. It should say whether `--archive` would run first, and where to. It is also the natural place to say what `destroy` does **not** remove. An operator is then not surprised later by what a removed campaign leaves on the host. SAC-032 is one case: each member's recorded agent session stays behind.

**How to see the gap.** Read `cs-campaign destroy --help` beside `cs-campaign create --help`.

**Not a regression.** `destroy` has never had this flag in this repository's history; it is filed as an improvement for that reason.
